record.name: Cuba
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Cuba approved a national AI development strategy in 2024 under the Ministry of Communications, with an advisory council and general risk-management and ethics principles.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. Recorded English and national or official-language queries and retrieved primary governance evidence support medium confidence. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

searches.query: Cuba estrategia inteligencia artificial instituto seguridad gobierno

check.language_note: The recorded es query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: CU-search = searches 1, 2 (en, es). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: UNESCO's national readiness assessment identifies the Ministry of Communications as lead for the National AI Strategy launched in 2024 and describes the existing legal framework and governance gaps. Its recommended multisectoral structures are not treated as existing bodies. The substantive Spanish text was retrieved through the saved reader-proxy copy after direct retrieval failed.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Communications (MINCOM)
related_bodies.role: It leads the national AI strategy and its advisory council; it provides general risk and impact oversight, and no model evaluation mandate was found.

record.notes:
Cited foreign sources for the governance context: OECD.AI Policy Navigator; UNESCO. The Ministry of Communications pages returned HTTP 403, so the strategy text was not read. OECD.AI describes general strategy oversight, including impact evaluation, AI-risk management and implementation supervision. A reported 22-member AI consortium was seen only in search results.

UNESCO's completed AI readiness assessment recommends multisector governance structures and legal updates. The recommended governance structures include international participation. Searches covered indexed public English and Spanish sources for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models.

next_check.reason: Retry the Ministry of Communications pages or the Gaceta Oficial for the strategy text.
